content.value_statement: Angular teams often struggle to choose the right RxJS operator and cleanup pattern. This skill gives practical patterns for reactive data flows, Signals interop, and error handling.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to convert Observables to Angular Signals with toSignal().
Explains when to use switchMap, mergeMap, concatMap, and combineLatest.
Provides examples for catchError, retry, and retryWhen flows.
Covers loading states, shared streams, polling, and WebSocket patterns.
limitations: It provides guidance only; it does not run or validate Angular code.
Examples use generic API paths and must be adapted to each project.
It does not replace security review for production HTTP calls.
It does not cover every RxJS operator or every Angular version.

use_cases.title: Modernize subscription cleanup
use_cases.description: Replace manual unsubscribe patterns with takeUntilDestroyed and Signals-friendly state handling.

use_cases.title: Design reactive search
use_cases.description: Build debounced search flows with distinctUntilChanged, switchMap, loading states, and error fallbacks.

use_cases.title: Review operator choices
use_cases.description: Compare RxJS operators and select patterns for parallel, sequential, cancellable, or combined streams.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple data stream
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an Angular component that loads data with HttpClient, converts it to a Signal, and handles an empty state.

prompt_templates.title: Add cleanup and error handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to refactor my Angular Observable flow so it uses takeUntilDestroyed, catchError, and a clear loading state.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor nested async logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to replace nested subscriptions with the right RxJS operators for cancellable requests, sequential work, and shared results.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a reactive feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a full Angular reactive feature with Signals, Observables, retry logic, polling, and clear error boundaries.

output_examples.input: I need a debounced search box in Angular.
output: Use a Signal for the input value and convert it to an Observable for stream operators.
Apply debounceTime, distinctUntilChanged, and switchMap so stale searches are canceled.
Convert the result stream back to a Signal for template rendering.

output_examples.input: Review this component that subscribes inside another subscription.
output: Identify the nested subscription as an anti-pattern because cleanup and errors become harder to manage.
Choose switchMap, concatMap, or mergeMap based on whether the work should cancel, queue, or run in parallel.
Add takeUntilDestroyed and local error handling before updating component state.

output_examples.input: Plan retry behavior for an Angular data load.
output: Use retry for simple transient failures and retryWhen for controlled backoff.
Stop retrying after a clear limit and return a safe fallback value.
Expose loading and error state separately from the successful data state.

best_practices: Prefer Signals for template state and RxJS for async stream composition.
Use takeUntilDestroyed for subscriptions created inside components or directives.
Handle errors inside streams and return explicit fallback values when appropriate.
anti_patterns: Do not nest subscriptions when an RxJS flattening operator can express the flow.
Do not leave manual subscriptions without a lifecycle cleanup strategy.
Do not share cached streams without understanding shareReplay reference counting.

faq.question: Does this skill execute code?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown guidance skill with Angular and RxJS examples.

faq.question: Which Angular versions does it target?
faq.answer: It targets modern Angular patterns that include Signals and the rxjs-interop package.

faq.question: Can it choose the correct RxJS operator?
faq.answer: It explains common operator choices and helps map use cases to operators.

faq.question: Does it cover subscription cleanup?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends takeUntilDestroyed for component and directive subscriptions.

faq.question: Can it help with HTTP error handling?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes catchError, retry, retryWhen, fallback values, and user-facing error state.

faq.question: Is it a replacement for testing?
faq.answer: No. Generated patterns still need project-specific tests and review.
